doc: The fleet-wide trigger cap (Khalid, 2026-11-02): no engine may start other engines, or itself, past these limits; past them the engines involved are held at reserved concurrency 0 under the spend governor's stage CAP and only an operator's {"action":"release_cap"} turns them back on.

Enforced by aws/shared/chain_guard.py at every start: system_events.publish, the event coordinator, chain_guard.lambda_client().invoke, chain_guard.chain_invoke. The module embeds a copy of this file; tests/deployment/test_trigger_cap.py fails the deploy if they differ.

handoff = an async start (Event invoke or bus event), the class that can multiply. call = a synchronous RequestResponse start (the caller waits). self = an engine re-invoking itself (the walkers; past max_self_hops they park, not breach).

Daily budgets are >= 2x each engine's busiest normal day of the 60 days to 2026-11-02 (ops 6717; the Oct 12-16 storm excluded) - the Invocations metric counts web and schedule runs too, so these are generous. Change a number here, redeploy chain_guard's importers, and it is live.

handoff.repeat_allowed_pairs: the only engine pairs that may visit each other again inside one chain - exactly the multi-engine invoke cycles of config/loop-allowlist.json (each with its stop condition; the gate keeps the two files equal). Depth, volume and the daily budgets still bound them, so an allowlisted exchange can never run away either.
